audit.whatIsWrong: Meditate is named twice (wants.foe[0] "Meditate stalling into his item spikes") but the entry never says it is a channel, and never tells Zac to break it.
audit.why: This is the largest single miss in the matchup. Meditate is a channel on a flat 10-second cooldown, and Zac carries three separate displacements - the Q knock-together, the E landing knockup, and four knockups on R. Any one of them ends the channel, and Yi then eats the full cooldown having healed almost nothing. Worse for him, Meditate also PAUSES the remaining duration on Wuju Style and Highlander while he channels, so interrupting it does not just deny the heal, it stops him banking ult time. The entry currently treats his sustain as something to be out-waited rather than something Zac is unusually well built to switch off.
audit.corrected: Added to whys[3], spikes[2].text, mid and wants.you[1].
sources: champ-data/_kits/masteryi.json (W flags channel, cooldown "10", "pause the remaining duration on Wuju Style and Highlander")

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text says "Let's Bounce keeps trades even - the repeated knockups interrupt his rhythm" without qualifying what R actually does through Highlander.
audit.why: Let's Bounce! does two things - it knocks up and it slows. Highlander makes Master Yi "immune to all slowing effects", so from level 6 the slow half of Zac's ultimate is simply deleted against him while the knockups still land. The line happens to point at the right half, but a player who does not know the slow is gone will misjudge every chase and disengage after 6.
audit.corrected: whys[4] and spikes[1].text now state that the knockups land and the slow does not.
sources: champ-data/_kits/masteryi.json (R "making him immune to all slowing effects")

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags "NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere" with 0 sequencing cues, and no number appears in the entry at all.
audit.why: Two concrete triggers exist and neither is stated. Alpha Strike is 20/19.5/19/18.5/18 but "basic attacks reduce Alpha Strike's cooldown", so the printed number is a ceiling and the read is his auto-attacks rather than a stopwatch - the same trap as Lucian's dash. And Highlander is a flat 85s at all three ranks, further reduced on any kill or assist, so it does not lengthen as the game goes on the way most ultimates do.
audit.corrected: Alpha Strike cooldown reduction added to whys[2] and early; the flat 85s Highlander added to late.
sources: champ-data/_kits/masteryi.json (Q "Basic attacks reduce Alpha Strike's cooldown", R cooldown "85" and "Passively reduces cooldown for his other abilities on a kill or assist")

audit.whatIsWrong: Alpha Strike is described only as damage Zac heals through; nothing says he is untargetable during it.
audit.why: Alpha Strike makes Yi untargetable for its duration. That is why it beats Zac's Q specifically - Q is a single-target grab, so a well-timed Alpha Strike does not merely dodge damage, it makes the grab impossible to land. wants.foe[1] already says "Alpha Strike dodging your Q and E engage" without explaining the mechanism that makes it work.

The chart (Zac / Zac / Skill / Skill / Skill / Master Yi / Master Yi) is consistent with the 49.39% win rate over 164 games - Zac ahead early, Yi ahead once items land, roughly even overall. No chart change proposed here, unlike most of this slice.
The existing "never sidelane him; engage his backline and let your team handle the Yi" is the right win condition and is already stated cleanly. Left as written.
